description: Agreacher wasn't born to be just a team. It was born to mean something and leave a mark on everyone it reaches. We came together with a shared passion and one goal: to succeed and create meaningful results. Agreacher is more than a tool; it is a helping hand, always there when you need it. We live for the love of the game.
summary:
When we think about space exploration, we usually remember the astronauts who went to the Moon, the rovers that explored Mars, or the incredible discoveries made along the way. But we rarely think about what happened to the machines that made these discoveries possible.

What happened to them after their missions ended? Where are they now? And do we ever stop to think about the things humanity has left behind in space?

These questions inspired us to create Orphans of Space.

We wanted to tell a different kind of space story. Instead of focusing only on successful missions and their achievements, we decided to look at the spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments that remained on the Moon, Mars, and beyond after their missions came to an end.

Our idea was to turn their stories into an interactive digital experience. Using NASA’s mission records, historical information, and scientific discoveries, we created a website where visitors can explore these forgotten explorers and learn about the legacy they left behind.

For us, this project is not just about machines or abandoned equipment. It is also about curiosity, discovery, and the incredible things humans have achieved by looking beyond Earth.

We hope that after exploring our website, people will look at space exploration a little differently and realize that even when a mission ends, its story doesn’t necessarily end with it.
details:
Orphans of Space takes visitors on a journey through the stories of human-made objects that remain beyond Earth.

We organized our story into four main chapters:

The Void: We begin by introducing the objects humanity has left behind in space and asking why their stories deserve to be remembered.

The Moon: We explore the equipment and scientific instruments left at the Apollo landing sites, showing how the first steps of human exploration created a lasting presence on the lunar surface.

The Rust: We travel to Mars and revisit robotic explorers such as Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity, remembering the missions that helped us understand our neighboring planet.

The Legacy: Finally, we look at what these missions left us: scientific knowledge, historical evidence, and a foundation for future exploration.

We also wanted visitors to do more than simply scroll through a story. That’s why we included interactive elements such as an artifact identification challenge and a timeline activity, allowing people to discover and test what they have learned.

We created Orphans of Space as an interactive, scroll-based website.

Our main focus was making the experience feel like a journey rather than a traditional educational webpage. As visitors scroll, the story develops chapter by chapter, combining visuals, historical information, and interactive elements.

The website includes:

•⁠ ⁠An interactive scrollytelling experience.

•⁠ ⁠A chapter-based narrative.

•⁠ ⁠Visual representations of space exploration history.

•⁠ ⁠An artifact identification challenge.

•⁠ ⁠An interactive mission timeline.

•⁠ ⁠Educational content based on NASA mission information.

A Different Perspective: We usually celebrate the beginning and success of space missions. We wanted to explore what happens after they end.

Storytelling Instead of Just Facts: Rather than presenting visitors with long lists of scientific information, we tried to make the history easier to understand through a story.

Learning Through Exploration: We included interactive activities so visitors could actively engage with the subject instead of just reading.

Real Stories, Real Missions: Our project is built around actual space missions and objects that still remain beyond Earth.

Connecting History and Science: We wanted to show that the legacy of space exploration continues even after individual missions are over.

We used PYTHON and ScrollyTelling AI tool to make our website.
